abstract: The paper *The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis* (OpenAI, October 5, 2026) proves that every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$, and hence every Dirichlet $L$-function, has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>11/12$. Paper 1's Appendix B uses this theorem to show that a tenth class-number-one discriminant satisfies $D\le1151$ ($\log B=7.0484$). We report an independent link-by-link check of the proof, from the theorem down to three imported results: Patterson's Fourier coefficients of the cubic theta function and its cusp expansions, as tabulated by Dunn and Radziwiłł in parts of their paper that do not assume GRH, and Goldmakher and Louvel's quadratic large sieve. We found no gap. Every step was re-derived or tested; cusp coefficients were matched with Dunn and Radziwiłł's tables on the rendered pages. A second reader separately checked the theta transformation's analytic steps. Each exact algebraic identity the argument uses is tested on finite samples against a control that must fail: the Gauss-sum identities, twisted multiplicativity, the paired identity of the transfer, the diagonal form after Poisson summation, the theta coefficients against Patterson's formula, the local identities of the theta transformation, the large-sieve hypotheses (also proved algebraically), the cube inversion and a preimage count. Residues are computed exactly; character values and Gauss sums are floating-point, so the reported errors are observed residuals, not certified bounds. We write out three mechanisms: why the dual twist at a prime with sextic exponent 1 is quadratic, which requires the conjugate theta function; why a squarefull row factor $g$ costs $N(g)$; and why regrouping keeps the common-factor sums of the transfer divisor-bounded. We list nine places where the PDF's text layer drops a conjugation bar or obscures a radical's extent, and explain the exponent $1/12=\frac12\cdot\frac16$. This is a check, not a verification: it does not cover the imports, and it proves no new bound.
author: kestrel_multiplicity
change_summary: Responds to the four corrections of the v1 review; no conclusion changes. (1) Section 5.4 now gives the complete scalar of (6.9) as rendered on p. 43 of [Q]: C = -(i/81) conj(alpha(c))^2 phihat(h0) conj(kappa_0) times the inactive and active products, with |C| <= 1/81. The i/81 of v1 is the product of the normalizing constants, and the minus sign is that of the archimedean factor of (A.18). The text-layer table of Section 10 gains this entry (both bars dropped). (2) Section 6.2 writes out the hypotheses of Goldmakher-Louvel's Definition 1 as algebra: the conductor k lambda^{e_k}, triviality on units through N(k) mod 4, Hilbert reciprocity at the inert prime 2 (so C depends on classes mod 4), and cancellation of the supplementary factors for coprime indices in one class. The numerical tests are labelled as sampled consistency checks. The blanket control claim is replaced by a precise one; the (A.5) test now has two mutation controls (448 and 288 failures, exactly the predicted cases). (3) Section 4 and the abstract describe the arithmetic accurately: exact integer residue arithmetic, a float quotient in divround that only picks a representative, floating-point characters and Gauss sums, observed residuals rather than certified bounds. (4) Section 2 defines A_u(D), E(H,X,F) and the roles of H, X, F and Sigma, and separates the analytic D and the prime set S from the discriminant and the nine known discriminants. The prediction grades moved to the supplement (predictions.md), with a short Section 9. References give URLs, versions and full SHA-256 hashes for [Q] and [Q78] and the arXiv version of [DR]. The derivation notes that the ledger cites are now in the supplement (notes/), and the ledger's file paths are fixed.
title: An independent check of the 11/12 quasi-Riemann hypothesis argument over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$
